title: Benchmark dataset master sheet (latency/$) — run index + validation status
content:
Redwood Inference — Public Benchmark Report (Latency/$) — Dataset Master Sheet
Owner: Mei Lin (data pipelines/validation)
Last refreshed: 2025-07-17
Dataset lock for v1.0 web/PDF: 2025-07-10 23:59 PT (anything after goes to v1.1 addendum)

What this sheet is
- The canonical run index used to generate the public benchmark JSON/CSV artifacts.
- One row = one benchmark “run” (model x region x workload config x runner build) that passed through validation.
- All public-facing charts/tables must map to a set of run_ids listed here with status=APPROVED_FOR_PUBLISH.

Key definitions (quick)
- prompt_set: v3-production-mix (see methodology page; includes prefill-heavy + decode-heavy prompts)
- workload_profile: A (balanced), B (prefill-heavy), C (decode-heavy)
- prefill_tokens / decode_tokens: target tokens; real outputs can vary slightly depending on stop conditions; see manifest.
- concurrency: number of simultaneous in-flight requests per runner.
- cache_policy: OFF (no prefix/KV reuse between requests). In-run caching internal to model execution is allowed.
- batching_policy: AUTO (runtime continuous batching enabled). If overridden, called out explicitly.
- p50_e2e_ms / p95_e2e_ms: end-to-end latency (client->server->client) from runner.
- throughput_tok_s: achieved output tokens/sec aggregated at runner.
- cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens: derived from metered GPU+platform cost attribution for the run window (see PR-4821 notes). Internal only but used to compute latency_per_dollar.
- latency_per_dollar_p50_ms_per_usd: normalization metric used by report. Lower is better.
- stability_gate: PASS if p95 variance <= threshold across repeats (see PR-4855). If FAIL, auto-rerun.
- validation_status: overall data quality outcome (see checklist). Only APPROVED_FOR_PUBLISH can ship.

IMPORTANT
- Do not quote single rows externally. Public claims are based on aggregated + rounded exports with disclaimers.
- If a run is marked EXCLUDED, it must not be referenced in narrative or charts.

Aggregation notes for PMM/web export
- Web exports aggregate across repeats for each (model, region, profile, context_tokens, concurrency) and then round.
- If multiple run_ids exist for the same cell, exports use the highest-quality APPROVED_FOR_PUBLISH run set (prefer repeats=3 and lowest p95_variance_pct).
- “Supported regions” list for publication is defined in Product thread 1749091188 (do not add a region to the landing page from this sheet alone).

- Confirm whether we want to publish the dedicated-pool sensitivity appendix (legal review pending; currently internal-only).
